yad-ephraim:1:_: There in Taz s.k. 4: we see in this correction of smeared plaster etc. — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:2:_: There: for lechi and not for tzurat hapetach for it is partition etc. — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:3:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 5: see siman 34 — thus it should read; meaning there in s.k. 37 he brought Tosafos' words that another lechi is required for pas does not help even though the pas is very wide and stands more than the breach since it protrudes three — see there as explained there:
yad-ephraim:4:_: Taz s.k. 13: One need not take anything for korah qualification of this matter we deal with like with bent where what bent is invalid — rather we view what is within ten as if it is not; and all this is not the topic here that one makes a wide korah from above and leaning below; and nevertheless it is obvious etc. — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:5:_: There in that s.k. below ten specifically — meaning that even though we would say Beit Yosef's view that if placed below ten it is invalid — meaning this would cause the permission; obviously this is invalid; rather Beit Yosef only said its head is above only that it is wide and extends somewhat below; but what Taz wrote on Bach and heaven forbid to say etc. — it appears he understood what Bach wrote that the concern is etc. — meaning concern to permit that one does not permit except within ten; and this is as Beit Yosef stated in his first explanation as above; and in truth Bach's intent in what he wrote that the concern is on the concern for prohibition — meaning Beit Yosef explains Rashba teaches us that leaning somewhat below is also valid lest one think otherwise that only if all is above ten is permitted — and he teaches us that even in such a case it is valid; and on this Bach objected that Rashba deals with a matter where the korah itself is wide ten tefachim and Taz's words require study:
yad-ephraim:6:_: There: and not all above ten and it is not so etc. that could not be written and the main point there is no printing error etc. — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:7:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 27: One should note the law of courtyard is not combined and requires etc. small paths between house and house etc. and tzurat hapetach is not required for this reason — it appears etc. as Magen Avraham wrote at the beginning of siman 364 in openings first — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:8:_: There: law of one who comes to divide etc. — meaning as explained in siman 392; and see below s.k. 34 and what Magen Avraham wrote if the mavo is not wide ten amot it is a printing error and must read more than ten amot; for if it is wide more than ten amot tzurat hapetach is specifically required; and what Magen Avraham wrote is only removal of residents — meaning since enclosed by wall there is no prohibition of carrying only because it is not combined that gentiles' mavo'ot open there and correction is needed there to remove gentiles' residents and two lechayim suffice as written; and from this reason also tzurat hapetach is not required in its bend since we say its law is like courtyard; and what Maharil wrote in responsum etc. and therefore two pasin are required etc. — meaning Maharil holds even in enclosed by wall it has no law of courtyard only karmelit law because gentiles have right of passage; and even though Maharil also agrees that two pasin or tzurat hapetach help to remove residents — nevertheless as long as residents are not removed it has law of karmelit and enclosure of wall does not make it reshut ha-yachid like uncombined courtyard; and Mahari Weil holds its law is like courtyard and the difference regarding broken on Shabbat as explained at end of siman 365 and automatically difference also for crooked mavo; and see what I wrote in pamphlet on responsum of Bach Chadashot siman 80:
yad-ephraim:9:_: Taz s.k. 19: To tie the rope from the side etc. — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:10:_: There: and it appears etc. — projections extend to nineteen near ground — perhaps he meant the projections begin near ground and go in height until ten tefachim; and perhaps printing error and must read projections nineteen until near ground; and in Mishbetzot Zahav it is written that it appears to him to emend until three — see there:
yad-ephraim:11:_: There: in place of reeds of tzurat hapetach and also etc. — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:12:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 37: and what Magen Avraham wrote — see siman 364 that on the other side two pasin suffice; in Sefer Tosafot Shabbos he expanded his words that here two pasin are required like courtyard and the sea questioned Darkhei Moshe for it implies tzurat hapetach is required and wrote perhaps specifically in complete mavo Magen Avraham speaks that lechi suffices; but here tzurat hapetach is required — end of his words; and this is not Magen Avraham's intent; and in my humble opinion Magen Avraham holds that even here lechi suffices; for even if it has law of courtyard nevertheless its breach is in ten and then tzurat hapetach is required; and if not two pasin suffice if four remained in one place or a tefach from here as explained above seif 2; and in our towns where on the fourth side also there are houses from this and that side — two pasin suffice when breach is not in ten and only lechi or korah is required because it has law of mavo and also in mavo law lechi or korah does not help if breached more than ten; and what Darkhei Moshe wrote I do not know the meaning; but I saw Darkhei Moshe wondered at Rashba that Bach brought and wrote that in courtyard tzurat hapetach does not help from here and lechi or korah from here but two pasin are required from the other side; and in my humble opinion the question on Rashba is when there is no breach in full and it is not in ten only open from two sides to reshut ha-rabbim where it is — then Rashba speaks well that tzurat hapetach is a complete partition and is not less than mavo where the other side is permitted with lechi or korah; and what is in the name of Maharil in responsum requires study; for Maharil siman 262 and Bach brought that he doubts perhaps lechi alone does not suffice — this is when open to gentiles' mavo'ot and from reason of removing residents as explained in his wording explicitly there; but regarding mavo qualification he agrees lechi alone suffices — see there; see in Tosafot who wrote with lechi or korah from here and even though lechi does not help in width ten — one may say he makes a wide lechi that reduces the hollow to ten etc.; and it must read that even though open to reshut ha-rabbim namely sixteen amot nevertheless the mavo itself is not wide sixteen only before the mavo there is reshut ha-rabbim from this and that; and what Tosafot wrote there daf 6 and daf 59 and see above siman 345 and in responsum I expanded on this matter:
yad-ephraim:13:_: There in s.k. 31 that Eimimar ruled in Sura in his responsum etc. — initially one may say that the mavo's correction is recognition lest one carry from there to the place of the sandbar, and so too Eliyah Rabbah; but below in siman 365 seif 5 it is stated: one should not sit at the head of the mavo with an object in his hand etc. — it appears this is not recognition lest one carry from reshut ha-rabbim there; and that which we say korah is for recognition does not mean recognition lest one carry from the mavo to reshut ha-rabbim etc. — rather recognition lest one come to carry in reshut ha-rabbim itself — see Rashi daf 3; and nevertheless there in siman 365 s.k. 11 Magen Avraham wrote it is possible tzurat hapetach is recognition regarding this concern lest one carry the object taken from his hand to reshut ha-yachid into the mavo; and if so here too tzurat hapetach would help; and as Magen Avraham wrote from Eimimar who made a complete partition; and it is possible Eimimar could not make a low tzurat hapetach because they needed to water camels through there — and similarly Tosafos wrote on daf 105 regarding let him make tzurat hapetach at the mouth of the path for camels come etc. — see there; and therefore he ruled in reshut ha-rabbim that he could easily remove it — as the Rav HaMaggid wrote — see there; and a high tzurat hapetach has no recognition concern as Magen Avraham wrote there s.k. 11 in siman 365; and accordingly what Magen Avraham wrote and tzurat hapetach does not help — meaning high specifically; but a low tzurat hapetach has recognition concern according to Magen Avraham himself whom I brought — requires study:
yad-ephraim:14:_: There in that seif tzurat hapetach even if it is etc. — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:15:_: In Taz s.k. 21 that he does not place diagonally except opposite the short — only regarding ten they dispute and we rule like Rava etc. — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:16:_: In Shulchan Aruch seif 31: there is a courtyard from the lechi outward etc. — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:17:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 34: except at one opening the entire city is permitted with these partitions — that opening's etc. — and one may qualify half — thus it should read:
yad-ephraim:18:_: Seif 36 in the gloss: and with this the mound counts as a partition — the language is garbled and explained for one who examines Beit Yosef — the Tur wrote that it rises in place of lechi and Beit Yosef wrote that according to lechi sufficing he wrote thus; but in truth the slope rises in place of a partition; but in any case there is no difference here whether it is like lechi or like a partition; and if so why is he precise and with this the mound counts as a partition; and what Beit Yosef wrote but the mound certainly that if it rose only in place of lechi it would not help at all since there are no partitions — rather the reason is because it rises in place of a partition for we say gud asik — end of his words; his intent is not that here regarding mavo qualification it would not help at all from the Torah it would not help since mavo is qualified by lechi; and even though lechi itself is for partition — nevertheless the mound that is ten high is like lechi and gud asik — why do I need; rather their intent is that there it discusses slope and mound and regarding mound we say if one threw and it landed on it he is liable; and on this Beit Yosef says if the mound had no other elevation only that it is like lechi it would not help at all — meaning for liability as he brought there before from Talmud and Rambam; and it is possible Beit Yosef is missing and must read it would not help at all to make him liable on it; and on this he says well since there are no partitions — meaning and if so what of it that it landed on it for behold there are no partitions around — only we say gud asik; thus appears Beit Yosef's explanation initially; and Rama's wording that wrote and with this etc. — it appears specifically in this we say it counts as a partition — requires study; and also here it deals only with slope and not mound; and even though Tur wrote in its wording that the mound rises in place of lechi and Beit Yosef wrote that for slope too they call mound for behold it is like a mound of earth — nevertheless Tur deals also with a complete mound — see there — and wrote mound including both; unlike here where it does not deal with mound at all; and why did he leave slope and write mound; and lest I fear a printing error fell in Rama and must read and likewise mound counts as a partition and the scribe erred and wrote in place of likewise with this and also separated the two heh of likewise and added by hand the word and with this the mound and this is a possible and common error; and his words revolve around what Beit Yosef wrote that in the Talmud mound was not mentioned for mavo only for throwing and Tosafot wrote mound also for mavo for they hold no difference and Rambam did not mention it only for throwing and not for not needing lechi — see there; and Rama intended to bring this law of Tosafot since the Mechaber wrote only Rambam's wording that mentioned only slope and not mound; and on this he wrote that likewise mound is as a partition; and nevertheless in Darkhei Moshe it is stated on Tosafot's words that the mound rises in place of lechi and Beit Yosef wrote and not in place of lechi but rises in place of a complete partition and so is proven from the Gemara — end of his words; it appears he also intended this in the gloss since he did not mention in Darkhei Moshe that word Beit Yosef wrote that even though only slope was mentioned not mound — Tur holds likewise mound; and nevertheless it is not far to say that here in the gloss he comes to write rulings and wrote this word that also with mound one need not lechi or korah:
